audit_scope.description: Batch 3 covers EL internal operations (bloom filters, KECCAK256, trace, RIPEMD160) and several EIPs (155, 1459, 8077, 2256, 2028) that define external interfaces for transaction submission, P2P discovery, and RPC APIs.

in_scope: Internal EVM operations (bloom, keccak, trace, RIPEMD160)

misclassified_entities.reason: Transaction Execution Engine in bloom.py is internal EL component producing logs, not an external entity crossing system boundary

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Transaction Submission)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC endpoint. All transaction data (signatures, calldata, gas parameters) must be validated. EIP-155 provides replay protection but does not authenticate users.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Asset Query)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated RPC endpoint. Query parameters (address, chainId, types) must be validated. User consent model assumes wallet-side authorization, not network-level trust.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p (Transaction Announcements)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P gossip network. Transaction announcement metadata (sender address, nonce) is explicitly untrusted per EIP-8077 security considerations. Used only as optimization hints, validated upon actual transaction retrieval.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network. All received blocks and block headers must undergo full consensus validation including PoW/PoS verification and state root verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS Infrastructure (Node Discovery)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: DNS TXT record queries (EIP-1459 enrtree protocol)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public DNS infrastructure is untrusted. EIP-1459 mitigates DNS poisoning via cryptographic signatures on TXT records (secp256k1), but DNS responses themselves are unauthenticated. Clients verify signatures and content hashes, but attackers can censor or delay responses.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transaction signature must be validated (ECDSA recovery, EIP-155 chain ID verification). Nonce must match account state. Balance must cover gas*price+value. Gas limit must cover intrinsic gas cost. Calldata gas must be correctly priced per EIP-2028 (16 gas/non-zero byte, 4 gas/zero byte).

Request parameters (address format, chainId validity) must be validated. User privacy requires wallet-side whitelisting before returning asset data. Justification parameter is untrusted user input for UI display only.

Announcement metadata (address, nonce) is untrusted and unverified. Used only for request prioritization. Actual transaction retrieved via GetPooledTransactions must undergo full validation. Protocol violation (metadata mismatch) should result in peer reputation penalty.

Block header must pass full validation: valid PoW/PoS proof, difficulty matches expected value, gas limit within bounds, timestamp reasonable, state root matches post-execution state. Ommers must be valid.

Root record signature must verify against known publisher public key (secp256k1). Sequence number must not decrease (replay protection). Branch/leaf content hashes must verify (keccak256). Multiple independent DNS sources should be used to mitigate eclipse attacks.
